verdict.rationale: The evidence documents a synchronous webhook only for real-time authorization decisions, plus an API for submitting and monitoring disputes. Nothing shows clearings, refunds, reversals or chargebacks arriving as webhooks, or stable transaction identifiers for ledger reconciliation. Auth webhooks and the dispute-submission API are adjacent features, not the post-auth event stream this story asks for.

support.subject: As a developer, post-auth events are as programmatic as auth — clearings, refunds, reversals, and chargebacks arrive as webhooks with stable transaction identifiers, so my own ledger never drifts
